user.title: Select your Godox light
user.description: Pick the light to connect to. Lights that look like Godox devices are listed first, but a provisioned Bluetooth Mesh node does not always advertise a recognizable name, so every connectable device is shown.

data_description.address: The light Home Assistant will keep its Bluetooth Mesh proxy connection to. Other lights on the same mesh network are reached through it.

setup_method.title: How is this light set up?
setup_method.description:
Has this light already been provisioned?

If you have run `godox-mesh provision`, choose **Use existing mesh keys** and paste your `mesh_state.json`.

If the light is factory reset and flashing, choose **Provision this light** to generate fresh keys here.

mesh_state.title: Mesh keys
mesh_state.description: Paste the full contents of the `mesh_state.json` file created by `godox-mesh provision`.

data_description.mesh_state_json: Must contain at least network_key and app_key. device_key, node_address, provisioner_address and iv_index are used when present.

provision.title: Provision this light
provision.description:
Put the light into pairing mode first — usually by holding its Bluetooth button until it flashes, though it varies by model. Whatever steps you would follow to pair it with the Godox app are the right ones here; it just has to be advertising as unprovisioned.

Home Assistant will generate a new network key and application key, run the Bluetooth Mesh provisioning exchange, and bind the key to the light's vendor model. This replaces any pairing with the Godox app.

model.title: Which model is this?
model.description: {detected}Pick the light's model so Home Assistant can give it the right controls — its colour-temperature range, or brightness only for a fixed-daylight light. Leave it blank if your model is not listed; the light will still work with a standard 2800–6500 K colour-temperature control.

data_description.radio_id: Search by product name. This sets the colour-temperature range and controls; it does not change the light's identity.
data_description.readback: Poll the light and show what it is really doing instead of what was last sent. Also adds a battery sensor on battery-powered lights.
data_description.poll_cct: Leave on unless the colour temperature shown does not match your light -- a few report a stale value after a change made on the light's own dial.
data_description.poll_interval: How often to ask the light for its state, in seconds.

join_existing.title: Add to an existing Godox mesh
join_existing.description:
Put the light into pairing mode first — usually by holding its Bluetooth button until it flashes, though it varies by model; it just has to be advertising as unprovisioned.

It will be provisioned onto your existing Godox mesh using the keys that network already uses, and controlled through the same connection as your other lights. No new entry is created.

data_description.mesh: Which of your Godox mesh networks to add this light to.

remove_node.title: Remove lights
remove_node.description: Select the lights to remove from this mesh network.

provision_node.title: Provision a new light
provision_node.description:
Put the light into pairing mode first — usually by holding its Bluetooth button until it flashes, though it varies by model. Whatever steps you would follow to pair it with the Godox app are the right ones here; it just has to be advertising as unprovisioned.

It will be provisioned onto this mesh network using the keys this entry already uses, and assigned unicast address {node_address}. It will then be controlled through the same connection as your other lights.

data_description.address: Only lights advertising as unprovisioned are listed. The light you set up first is not listed — it is already on this network.
data_description.name: Optional. Shown in Home Assistant, for example Fill Light. If left blank, the model name is used.
